<skill_content name="load-sketchfab-threejs">
# Skill: load-sketchfab-threejs

# Load Sketchfab models into Three.js and PlayCanvas

Use the bundled downloader, inspector, safe normalizer, and A/B viewer. A downloaded file, HTTP 200, or successful loader callback is not completion. Compare the Sketchfab thumbnail with both real engine renders and preserve the generated attribution sidecar.

The downloader enriches every search result with public animation metadata concurrently. Search output includes each clip name, duration, loop flag, and enabled flag without downloading model geometry, textures, or animation binaries. Use `--no-animations` to skip this enrichment or `--animation-workers 1..24` to tune concurrency. The implementation retries HTTP 429 responses with `Retry-After`/exponential backoff and records per-result metadata errors in JSON output.

Every search also creates a visual contact sheet, `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` by default, plus a same-name `.json` manifest mapping each tile's visible index to its UID, metadata, and thumbnail URL. Use `--preview-sheet /absolute/path/results.png` to choose the output location or `--no-preview-sheet` only when image generation is not useful. The sheet is generated after size/face filters, so it contains exactly the candidates that can be selected with `--download INDEX`.

Searches target non-downloadable Sketchfab models by default. Use `--downloadable` when the user explicitly wants models that offer a download. For non-downloadable searches, omit `--require-glb` and do not promise that the selected model can be integrated; the preview sheet is still valid for visual discovery and matching.

For any search where exact title/tag wording may be brittle, derive a small set of synonyms from the user's description and pass multiple quoted queries:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" \
  "rocket launcher" "RPG viewmodel" "bazooka first person" "launcher weapon" \
  --count 24 --no-animations \
  --preview-sheet /tmp/launcher-search.png
```

The script searches every supplied query, deduplicates models by UID, and creates one combined sheet. Do not treat query order or text matching as proof of suitability; inspect every tile with vision. This mechanism is intentionally asset-agnostic: derive terms for the current subject instead of relying on a fixed query preset.

Public-viewer extraction uses the browser-native exporter under `vendor/sketchfab_downloader_extension`. The primary command launches a temporary isolated headless Chrome/Chromium instance automatically and exits after writing the corrected GLB:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/extract_public_model.py" \
  "https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/example-UID" \
  --output /absolute/project/public/models/model.glb
```

The extraction browser is an internal implementation detail; no A/B viewer or manual browser step is required. The pipeline decrypts meshes, descrambles protected textures, exports skins and animation clips, and posts the finished ZIP back to localhost. The bridge extracts the single GLB and automatically creates `<model>.glb.attribution.json` beside it using `/i/models/{uid}` metadata. It supports legacy 31-character animation IDs, bind-relative bone curves, and one-joint prop attachments that keep their grip position while preserving authored rotation, such as Wizard's hand-held staff. If the metadata endpoint provides no license, record the license as `CC`. Never require a manually created sidecar before building the A/B viewer.

## Keep the test lightweight

Set the skill path once:

```sh
SKILL_DIR="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs"
```

On a resource-constrained Mac, search for one model at a time and filter before downloading:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb
```

Open the generated `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` with vision before selecting a result. Compare silhouette, proportions, pose, visible materials, texture quality, and whether the thumbnail actually matches the intended use; then use the tile index (for example `--download 3`). Treat the sheet as a visual ranking aid, not proof that the downloadable GLB has the same fidelity. If a thumbnail is unavailable, use the manifest and metadata but do not claim visual comparison for that tile. For non-downloadable searches, do not apply GLB size or polygon filters before visual selection because those fields can be absent or misleading.

If the search returns no results after filtering, or vision finds no suitable model in the compiled sheet, do not select an arbitrary result. Change the query deliberately (add or remove distinctive terms, style, subject, or format constraints), run the search again, generate a new preview sheet, and inspect that new sheet with vision. Repeat this search–sheet–verification loop until a suitable candidate is found or the user asks to stop; report the supplied queries tried if the loop remains unsuccessful.

Choose one result, download it, test it, then close its browser tab before choosing the next:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb --downloadable \
  --download 0 --output /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Use the built-in Sketchfab token pool by default. `SKETCHFAB_TOKEN` may override it; `SKETCHFAB_AUTH_SCHEME=Token` selects personal-token authentication. Never print token values. Keep `tree.glb.attribution.json` beside `tree.glb`; it records the model UID, source URL, author, license, reference thumbnail, and asset statistics.

Prefer CC Attribution results when choices are otherwise similar. Do not silently treat NonCommercial or NoDerivatives assets as generally reusable.

## Inspect before integration

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/inspect_glb.mjs" /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Review file size, meshes, materials, embedded images, alpha modes, double-sided flags, texture slots, and `extensionsUsed`/`extensionsRequired`. Prefer GLB because it keeps buffers and textures together.

Treat these as compatibility signals:

- `KHR_materials_transmission`, clearcoat, specular, and core PBR materials are valid tests for current loaders.
- `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness` is archived. Three.js may load geometry while dropping its diffuse textures.
- `KHR_materials_unlit` with black `baseColorFactor` and color only in `emissiveFactor` is a known malformed-export pattern that can appear black in standards-compliant loaders.
- Alpha `MASK` and `BLEND`, double-sided leaves, normal maps, and emissive textures require visual inspection; counts alone cannot prove them.

## Normalize only safe legacy patterns

Run the normalizer only after inspection or a visible A/B mismatch:

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/normalize_glb.mjs" input.glb --output normalized.glb
```

The normalizer:

- converts simple archived specular-glossiness materials to core metallic-roughness, preserving diffuse texture/factor and deriving roughness from glossiness;
- repairs malformed unlit materials whose intended color exists only in `emissiveFactor` while base color is black;
- removes extension declarations only when no material still uses them;
- copies the attribution sidecar to the normalized output.

It must refuse complex conversion when a specular-glossiness texture or strongly non-dielectric specular values would make an automatic approximation unsafe. Keep the original GLB and report that a conversion was performed.

## Build the isolated A/B viewer

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/prepare_viewer.py" \
  --model /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb \
  --output /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
python3 -m http.server 8765 --directory /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` through HTTP, never `file://`. The viewer shows the Sketchfab reference thumbnail and a Three.js preview:

1. Sketchfab reference thumbnail.
2. Three.js with the official matching `GLTFLoader` addon.

Original materials are the default. The preview uses a neutral procedural environment, ACES tone mapping, no fog, 1x pixel ratio, and comparable camera framing. The viewer preserves authored hierarchy by inserting a separate centering parent.

Useful diagnostic URLs:

- `?only=three` loads the Three.js preview for a lower-memory check.
- `?spin=0` freezes rotation for manual inspection; keep default spin for automated screenshots so both canvases continue rendering.
- `?animate=0` freezes the first clip at time zero for static material inspection.

## Browser acceptance

Wait until `document.body.dataset.compareState` is `ready`. Inspect each panel's `data-details` JSON and confirm:

- reference and Three.js say `Rendered`;
- Three.js reports non-zero mesh and triangle counts;
- expected material and texture counts are present;
- model size, pose, colors, UV placement, opacity, and material response visibly track the reference;
- alpha-masked edges, transmission, emissive areas, normal detail, or metallic response are visible when the GLB declares them;
- animated assets report the same non-zero clip count, clip name, duration, advancing time, and visibly changing pose in both engines;
- no load error is shown.

Capture a screenshot containing all three columns and the statistics. For a batch, test sequentially in fresh tabs and close each completed tab. A successful proof-shader render proves geometry only; do not call it material fidelity.

## Engine integration

For Three.js projects, use the project's installed Three.js version and its matching addon:

```js
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';

const gltf = await new GLTFLoader().loadAsync('/models/tree.glb');
scene.add(gltf.scene);
```

Update world matrices before measuring `THREE.Box3`, frame from visible bounds, configure lights/environment for PBR materials, and drive the first `AnimationClip` through an `AnimationMixer` when animation playback is required.

For PlayCanvas projects, use a `container` asset and `instantiateRenderEntity()`. Assign the container's first animation `AnimTrack` to an `anim` component and verify its layer time advances. Synchronize hierarchy before reading mesh-instance bounds. Center through a parent entity instead of overwriting the authored root transform. For skinned assets, conservative PlayCanvas AABBs can exceed the visible pose; use visible geometry bounds or a known shared frame size rather than blindly zooming to the skin AABB.

## Failure guide

- White Three.js model but textured PlayCanvas model: inspect for archived `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness`; normalize if the converter accepts it.
- Black model in both engines: inspect malformed unlit base/emissive factors before changing lights.
- PlayCanvas model tiny but Three.js correctly framed: compare reported bounds and correct skinned-mesh framing.
- Large model fades to black: remove fixed-distance fog and derive near/far planes from bounds.
- Ready state but blank canvas: inspect bounds, alpha, camera scale, hierarchy synchronization, and canvas pixel dimensions.
- Missing textures: use GLB or preserve every `.gltf` relative URI.
- Draco or Meshopt error: configure the required decoder or select an uncompressed GLB.
- Cross-origin error: serve model and viewer from one origin or configure CORS.

## Completion standard

Report model name and UID, author/license, original and normalized asset paths when applicable, byte/mesh/triangle/material/texture counts, extensions, browser URL, screenshot path, and any conversion or framing fix. Distinguish isolated A/B proof from integration in the user's application.

# VERDANT: The Pixel Wound — Game Design Document

**Version:** Prototype 0.1 · **Genre:** Third-person action RPG / ecological choice adventure · **Platform:** Browser (desktop and touch)

## High concept

The Pixel Virus is converting a living forest into a luminous, geometric ecosystem. As the Wayfarer, fight the creatures it mutates, recover fragments of digital matter, and decide the fate of each infection wound. Purification restores the forest and ends the threat; planting a Pixel Seed halts the spread but preserves a strange, productive sanctuary. Neither choice is a simple upgrade: restoration protects familiar life, while stabilization accepts permanent change in exchange for rare resources and a living frontier.

## Player promise and pillars

1. **Readable, responsive melee:** make space, choose a weapon, recognize enemy attack tells, and commit to a short combo or a timed defense.
2. **A world that visibly reacts:** infection has a radius and lifecycle, animals can mutate inside it, and vegetation, ground effects, and HUD indicators react to its state.
3. **A meaningful ecological decision:** after defeating a zone's guardians, purify it or spend a scarce seed to preserve a contained pixel biome.
4. **Immediate, low-friction play:** no install or account; keyboard/mouse and touch alternatives are available from the same browser build.

## Core gameplay loop

1. Approach the Mosswound and observe its orange infection boundary, expanding voxel flora, and monster count.
2. Switch between sword, spear, and shield to suit the engagement. Use movement and dodge to avoid attacks; parry on the wind-up or block while facing an attacker.
3. Defeat the guardians. They drop floating Pixel Shards that can be harvested at close range.
4. Enter the wound and choose **Purify** or **Plant a Pixel Seed**. Purification takes several seconds and shrinks the radius to nothing. Seeding immediately arrests expansion but leaves pixel flora, periodic shard deposits, and occasional returning beasts.
5. Explore the resulting ecosystem and use the recovered fragments as a future crafting currency (crafting is a planned extension, not implemented in the prototype).

## Controls

| Action | Desktop | Touch |
|---|---|---|
| Move | WASD / arrow keys | Direction pad |
| Attack / combo | Space, J, or left mouse | HIT |
| Dodge | Shift | DODGE |
| Block | Hold right mouse button | — (use dodge as the mobile defense) |
| Parry | Q | — |
| Switch weapon | 1 / 2 / 3 or weapon buttons | Weapon buttons |
| Purify | E | ACT when the zone is clear |
| Plant a seed | F | Keyboard/compatible external controls; shown in field manual |
| Harvest nearby shard | R | ACT near a shard |
| Field manual | ? button | ? button |

## Combat design

- **Sword — Ashen Sword:** balanced range and high damage; its three-hit chain rewards continuous attacks during the combo window.
- **Spear — March Spear:** long reach and moderate damage; slower recovery and stamina cost favor spacing.
- **Shield — Bulwark Shield:** short-range bash; holding right mouse reduces incoming frontal damage substantially. A block drains stamina. A block from behind does not protect the player.
- **Parry:** Q opens a brief timing window. A successful frontal parry negates the hit and staggers the attacker, creating a punish opportunity. A mistimed parry leaves the player vulnerable.
- **Dodge:** a short burst with a temporary invulnerability window, paid for with stamina.
- **Stamina:** regenerates outside of strenuous actions. Attacks, blocks, and dodges spend it; empty stamina discourages defensive spamming.
- **Recovery:** defeat restores the Wayfarer at the trailhead with partial stamina, keeping the prototype playable without a hard reset.

## Infection-zone state model

`InfectionZone` is the authoritative simulation object. Its state is separate from Three.js meshes; render objects read radius and state and update their indicators.

| State | Spread | Visual treatment | Gameplay |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SPREADING` | Radius expands to its cap; mutation checks can convert animals in the boundary. | Warm orange ring and halo, grid, voxel growth, floating blocks. | Guardians defend the zone. Once cleared, either outcome is available. |
| `PURIFYING` | Expansion stops; the radius contracts over a short channel. | Ring shifts toward green; voxel growth recedes with the boundary. | The Wayfarer must remain safe long enough for recovery to finish. |
| `PURIFIED` | Permanently stopped; radius is zero. | Boundary and pixel field vanish; organic clearing is revealed. | The infection cannot repopulate. The restorative outcome is permanent. |
| `SEEDED` | Permanently stopped. | Cool cyan boundary and retained pixel sanctuary. | Periodic shard deposits and a limited number of returning stalkers sustain the resource loop. |

The state transition is one-way in the prototype: `SPREADING → PURIFYING → PURIFIED` or `SPREADING → SEEDED`. A seed is a limited inventory choice. Zone HUD state, radius, threat count, progress, prompt, color, and scene visibility all derive from the same state to avoid contradictory presentation.

## Pixel Monsters

These are the prototype's three readable combat archetypes. The game uses procedural primitive meshes; the silhouettes and palette are intentionally distinct enough to support later replacement with authored models.

| Monster | Behavior | Prototype combat profile | Drop |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Moss Stalker** | Hunts the Wayfarer and closes at a steady pace; a balanced baseline foe. | 45 HP, medium speed, 14 damage, 2.25 m/s pursuit. | 2 Pixel Shards. |
| **Brambleback** | Heavy, broad-bodied guardian; slow approach, high impact, and more health. A mutated stag can become one. | 70 HP, slow pursuit, 23 damage, 1.65 m/s pursuit. | 4 Pixel Shards. |
| **Shardling** | Small, low silhouette with a fast approach and quick, low-damage attacks. | 45 HP, fast pursuit, 9 damage, 3.35 m/s pursuit. | 1 bright Pixel Shard. |

All foes use a short wind-up before an attack so the player can read, dodge, block, or parry. Prototype values are tuning starting points, not final balance targets.

## World and visual direction

- **Setting:** a quiet, moss-rich woodland trail around one central wound, framed by natural conifers and a clearing.
- **Organic state:** subdued fern greens, warm bark, soft daylight, distant atmospheric fog, and small wandering animals.
- **Infected state:** hard-edged cuboid growths and floating fragments in mint, cyan, and acid green; a warm boundary makes the danger radius legible against the cooler infection palette.
- **Seeded state:** the cyan ring communicates containment rather than cure. Pixel geometry remains visible, and the zone becomes a repeatable resource frontier.
- **Purified state:** the infected geometry, field, grid, and boundary disappear; the clearing returns to the surrounding organic palette.
- **Interface:** compact dark glass panels, monospaced field labels, clear resource counts, contextual prompts, and an optional field manual. The HUD is kept within safe areas on narrow screens.
- **Asset policy for this prototype:** procedural Three.js geometry and built-in materials only; no external model dependency.

## Audio direction (planned)

A restrained forest ambience should give way to a soft digital shimmer near infection. Monster wind-ups need distinct, short tells. Purification should resolve with a warm, organic swell; seeding should use a crystalline locking tone. Audio is not yet implemented.

## Scope and implementation notes

**Implemented prototype:** one forest clearing and one infection zone; spreading/mutation hooks; three monster archetypes; simple pursuit and telegraphed melee; weapon switching, combos, block/parry/dodge; shard drops and collection; purify/seed outcomes; responsive HUD, field manual, keyboard/mouse and touch movement/action controls.

**Planned beyond this prototype:** multiple connected zones, branching narrative, crafting, permanent save data, authored character/monster assets, richer animal mutation and restoration behaviors, audio, mobile touch parry/block buttons, and accessibility settings. Seeded-zone population is a lightweight repeating encounter loop, not a full ecology simulation.

## Prototype acceptance checks

- The scene renders and updates continuously in a modern browser.
- Player can move, switch all three weapons, chain attacks, dodge, block, and parry.
- Monsters pursue, attack after a readable wind-up, and drop harvestable shards on defeat.
- The active zone grows and updates its indicators; animals inside can mutate into beasts.
- With guardians defeated, purify completes and removes the pixel wound, or planting a seed arrests spread while retaining a resource-generating sanctuary.
- HUD and controls remain legible at desktop and mobile widths.

- Build a complete, playable browser-based third-person action RPG prototype about a Pixel Virus infecting a forest, with combat and a Purify-versus-Pixel-Seed choice.

- Use procedural Three.js geometry without external model assets.
- Inspect only the latest screenshot.

- Use a browser-based Three.js prototype with a custom HTML/CSS HUD.
- Model the infection lifecycle with spreading, purifying, seeded, and purified states, with visual indicator hooks.

- Validate runtime behavior and gameplay in a browser; fix any issues found.
- Capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot at or below 1280px wide.

- Browser validation and screenshot capture have not yet been completed.

- `game.js`: Three.js scene, infection-zone state, combat, player and monster updates, HUD, and render loop.
- `index.html`: Game shell and UI.

## Objective
- Complete and validate a playable browser-based third-person action RPG prototype about a Pixel Virus infecting a forest, including combat and a Purify-versus-Seed choice.
- Document the design and capture and inspect a JPEG screenshot at a viewport no wider than 1280px.

## Requirements
- Include sword, spear, and shield switching; combos; blocking, parrying, and dodging.
- Infection zones spread and mutate animals into Pixel Monsters; defeated zones can be purified or stabilized with a Pixel Seed.
- Cover three monster archetypes and drops, plus visual transitions between organic, infected, and stabilized environments.

1: # VERDANT: The Pixel Wound — Game Design Document
2: 
3: **Version:** Prototype 0.1 · **Genre:** Third-person action RPG / ecological choice adventure · **Platform:** Browser (desktop and touch)
4: 
5: ## High concept
6: 
7: The Pixel Virus is converting a living forest into a luminous, geometric ecosystem. As the Wayfarer, fight the creatures it mutates, recover fragments of digital matter, and decide the fate of each infection wound. Purification restores the forest and ends the threat; planting a Pixel Seed halts the spread but preserves a strange, productive sanctuary. Neither choice is a simple upgrade: restoration protects familiar life, while stabilization accepts permanent change in exchange for rare resources and a living frontier.
8: 
9: ## Player promise and pillars
10: 
11: 1. **Readable, responsive melee:** make space, choose a weapon, recognize enemy attack tells, and commit to a short combo or a timed defense.
12: 2. **A world that visibly reacts:** infection has a radius and lifecycle, animals can mutate inside it, and vegetation, ground effects, and HUD indicators react to its state.
13: 3. **A meaningful ecological decision:** after defeating a zone's guardians, purify it or spend a scarce seed to preserve a contained pixel biome.
14: 4. **Immediate, low-friction play:** no install or account; keyboard/mouse and touch alternatives are available from the same browser build.
15: 
16: ## Core gameplay loop
17: 
18: 1. Approach the Mosswound and observe its orange infection boundary, expanding voxel flora, and monster count.
19: 2. Switch between sword, spear, and shield to suit the engagement. Use movement and dodge to avoid attacks; parry on the wind-up or block while facing an attacker.
20: 3. Defeat the guardians. They drop floating Pixel Shards that can be harvested at close range.
21: 4. Enter the wound and choose **Purify** or **Plant a Pixel Seed**. Purification takes several seconds and shrinks the radius to nothing. Seeding immediately arrests expansion but leaves pixel flora, periodic shard deposits, and occasional returning beasts.
22: 5. Explore the resulting ecosystem and use the recovered fragments as a future crafting currency (crafting is a planned extension, not implemented in the prototype).
23: 
24: ## Controls
25: 
26: | Action | Desktop | Touch |
27: |---|---|---|
28: | Move | WASD / arrow keys | Direction pad |
29: | Attack / combo | Space, J, or left mouse | HIT |
30: | Dodge | Shift | DODGE |
31: | Block | Hold right mouse button | — (use dodge as the mobile defense) |
32: | Parry | Q | — |
33: | Switch weapon | 1 / 2 / 3 or weapon buttons | Weapon buttons |
34: | Purify | E | ACT when the zone is clear |
35: | Plant a seed | F | Keyboard/compatible external controls; shown in field manual |
36: | Harvest nearby shard | R | ACT near a shard |
37: | Field manual | ? button | ? button |
38: 
39: ## Combat design
40: 
41: - **Sword — Ashen Sword:** balanced range and high damage; its three-hit chain rewards continuous attacks during the combo window.
42: - **Spear — March Spear:** long reach and moderate damage; slower recovery and stamina cost favor spacing.
43: - **Shield — Bulwark Shield:** short-range bash; holding right mouse reduces incoming frontal damage substantially. A block drains stamina. A block from behind does not protect the player.
44: - **Parry:** Q opens a brief timing window. A successful frontal parry negates the hit and staggers the attacker, creating a punish opportunity. A mistimed parry leaves the player vulnerable.
45: - **Dodge:** a short burst with a temporary invulnerability window, paid for with stamina.
46: - **Stamina:** regenerates outside of strenuous actions. Attacks, blocks, and dodges spend it; empty stamina discourages defensive spamming.
47: - **Recovery:** defeat restores the Wayfarer at the trailhead with partial stamina, keeping the prototype playable without a hard reset.
48: 
49: ## Infection-zone state model
50: 
51: `InfectionZone` is the authoritative simulation object. Its state is separate from Three.js meshes; render objects read radius and state and update their indicators.
52: 
53: | State | Spread | Visual treatment | Gameplay |
54: |---|---|---|---|
55: | `SPREADING` | Radius expands to its cap; mutation checks can convert animals in the boundary. | Warm orange ring and halo, grid, voxel growth, floating blocks. | Guardians defend the zone. Once cleared, either outcome is available. |
56: | `PURIFYING` | Expansion stops; the radius contracts over a short channel. | Ring shifts toward green; voxel growth recedes with the boundary. | The Wayfarer must remain safe long enough for recovery to finish. |
57: | `PURIFIED` | Permanently stopped; radius is zero. | Boundary and pixel field vanish; organic clearing is revealed. | The infection cannot repopulate. The restorative outcome is permanent. |
58: | `SEEDED` | Permanently stopped. | Cool cyan boundary and retained pixel sanctuary. | Periodic shard deposits and a limited number of returning stalkers sustain the resource loop. |
59: 
60: The state transition is one-way in the prototype: `SPREADING → PURIFYING → PURIFIED` or `SPREADING → SEEDED`. A seed is a limited inventory choice. Zone HUD state, radius, threat count, progress, prompt, color, and scene visibility all derive from the same state to avoid contradictory presentation.
61: 
62: ## Pixel Monsters
63: 
64: These are the prototype's three readable combat archetypes. The game uses procedural primitive meshes; the silhouettes and palette are intentionally distinct enough to support later replacement with authored models.
65: 
66: | Monster | Behavior | Prototype combat profile | Drop |
67: |---|---|---|---|
68: | **Moss Stalker** | Hunts the Wayfarer and closes at a steady pace; a balanced baseline foe. | 45 HP, medium speed, 14 damage, 2.25 m/s pursuit. | 2 Pixel Shards. |
69: | **Brambleback** | Heavy, broad-bodied guardian; slow approach, high impact, and more health. A mutated stag can become one. | 70 HP, slow pursuit, 23 damage, 1.65 m/s pursuit. | 4 Pixel Shards. |
70: | **Shardling** | Small, low silhouette with a fast approach and quick, low-damage attacks. | 45 HP, fast pursuit, 9 damage, 3.35 m/s pursuit. | 1 bright Pixel Shard. |
71: 
72: All foes use a short wind-up before an attack so the player can read, dodge, block, or parry. Prototype values are tuning starting points, not final balance targets.
73: 
74: ## World and visual direction
75: 
76: - **Setting:** a quiet, moss-rich woodland trail around one central wound, framed by natural conifers and a clearing.
77: - **Organic state:** subdued fern greens, warm bark, soft daylight, distant atmospheric fog, and small wandering animals.
78: - **Infected state:** hard-edged cuboid growths and floating fragments in mint, cyan, and acid green; a warm boundary makes the danger radius legible against the cooler infection palette.
79: - **Seeded state:** the cyan ring communicates containment rather than cure. Pixel geometry remains visible, and the zone becomes a repeatable resource frontier.
80: - **Purified state:** the infected geometry, field, grid, and boundary disappear; the clearing returns to the surrounding organic palette.
81: - **Interface:** compact dark glass panels, monospaced field labels, clear resource counts, contextual prompts, and an optional field manual. The HUD is kept within safe areas on narrow screens.
82: - **Asset policy for this prototype:** procedural Three.js geometry and built-in materials only; no external model dependency.
83: 
84: ## Audio direction (planned)
85: 
86: A restrained forest ambience should give way to a soft digital shimmer near infection. Monster wind-ups need distinct, short tells. Purification should resolve with a warm, organic swell; seeding should use a crystalline locking tone. Audio is not yet implemented.
87: 
88: ## Scope and implementation notes
89: 
90: **Implemented prototype:** one forest clearing and one infection zone; spreading/mutation hooks; three monster archetypes; simple pursuit and telegraphed melee; weapon switching, combos, block/parry/dodge; shard drops and collection; purify/seed outcomes; responsive HUD, field manual, keyboard/mouse and touch movement/action controls.
91: 
92: **Planned beyond this prototype:** multiple connected zones, branching narrative, crafting, permanent save data, authored character/monster assets, richer animal mutation and restoration behaviors, audio, mobile touch parry/block buttons, and accessibility settings. Seeded-zone population is a lightweight repeating encounter loop, not a full ecology simulation.
93: 
94: ## Prototype acceptance checks
95: 
96: - The scene renders and updates continuously in a modern browser.
97: - Player can move, switch all three weapons, chain attacks, dodge, block, and parry.
98: - Monsters pursue, attack after a readable wind-up, and drop harvestable shards on defeat.
99: - The active zone grows and updates its indicators; animals inside can mutate into beasts.
100: - With guardians defeated, purify completes and removes the pixel wound, or planting a seed arrests spread while retaining a resource-generating sanctuary.
101: - HUD and controls remain legible at desktop and mobile widths.

## Objective
- Finish and validate the playable browser-based third-person action RPG prototype about a Pixel Virus infecting a forest, including combat and a Purify-versus-Seed choice.
- Document the design and capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot at a viewport no wider than 1280px.

## Requirements
- Include sword, spear, and shield switching; combos; blocking, parrying, and dodging.
- Infection zones spread and mutate animals into Pixel Monsters; defeated zones can be purified or stabilized with a Pixel Seed.
- Cover three monster archetypes and drops, plus visual transitions between organic, infected, and stabilized environments.
- Use procedural Three.js geometry without external model assets.
- Inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use a browser-based Three.js prototype with a custom HTML/CSS HUD.
- Model infection lifecycle states as spreading, purifying, seeded, and purified.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the game shell, HUD, field guide, weapon slots, controls, responsive styling, procedural Three.js scene, combat and infection logic, and `GDD.md`.
- Confirmed the game loads in Chromium; weapon hotkeys switch to spear and shield.
- Checked the mobile layout at 390×844: touch controls are visible, with no horizontal or vertical overflow.
- Captured `screenshots/verdant-latest.jpg` at 1024×768; it may show the guide overlay.

### Active
- Validate the latest `game.js` changes: player spawn location, combat target-facing assistance, and delayed animal mutation.
- Verify guide visibility and combat; test weapon actions, both zone outcomes, shard harvesting, and mobile touch actions.
- Recheck desktop and mobile layouts, then recapture and inspect only the newest JPEG.

### Blocked
- Combat and infection transitions remain unverified end to end; earlier attacks did not reduce threats, which rose from 3 to 6 as monsters spawned.
- Starting the preview with `PORT=3000 ./start.sh` failed with `EADDRINUSE`; port 3000 is already occupied.

## Next Move
1. Open the existing preview on its active port or start the project on an available port, then reload and verify the latest `game.js` changes.
2. Test blocking, parrying, dodging, shard harvesting, and both Purify and Seed lifecycle outcomes; check mobile touch actions.
3. Recheck guide panel behavior and responsive layouts, then capture and inspect only the newest JPEG at a viewport no wider than 1280px.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: scene, player and monster behavior, combat, and infection-zone states; recent changes remain unverified.
- `index.html`: HUD, guide panel, and touch controls.
- `style.css`: HUD and responsive layouts.
- `GDD.md`: game design document.
- `screenshots/verdant-latest.jpg`: latest screenshot; potentially stale and may include the guide overlay.
- `start.sh`: preview startup script; the attempted port 3000 was occupied.
- `capture.sh`: screenshot capture script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- Recent `game.js` edits moved the initial player position from z=15 to z=10, delayed animal mutation until 24 seconds and no living monsters remain, and made attacks face the nearest monster within attack reach plus 2.
- Browser console previously reported a missing `/favicon.ico` (404) and WebGL readback performance warnings.
